text:
marta: Heads-up: we started seeing a spike in fncall schema rejections after last night's runtime change. ~0.4% of calls are getting rejected with ValidatorError(missing_field) from fncall_validator.v1 :eyes:
kevin: ugh. Do we have an example payload + error?
sam: My quick grep shows the failures are concentrated on a single route (/summarize/v2) and around 03:12-03:18 UTC. Likely a model variant returned slightly different structure.
marta: here's one of the rejection logs (sanitized):
```json
{
  "request_id": "req_8c7a",
  "model": "open-prod-19b",
  "tool": "summarizer.exact",
  "tool_output": { "summary_text": "..." },
  "validator_error": "Missing required key 'result' in tool_output"
}
```
julia: that looks like the model returned summary_text instead of result.{text,score} which explains missing_field. The schema expects tool_output.result to be an object.
elaine: two things we need: 1) stop customer-facing 5xxs and 2) get telemetry so we can triage without storing PII. Proposal: fallback routing to a compatible model variant when schema validator fails, and surface a lightweight error code in the response.
kevin: agree on fallback. Option A: automatic silent fallback to fallback_model for that route (costly). Option B: return a 200 with a wrapper {"status":"schema_rejected","reason":"missing_field","hint":"use model:open-stable-7b or enable lenient_mode"} so caller can handle.
marta: we must not return raw tool output to customers for security. But a short error code + non-sensitive hint is ok. Also we should emit a telemetry event: fncall.schema.reject with tags: route=/summarize/v2, model=open-prod-19b, reason=missing_field, rollout_group=canary-1.
ops-bot: alert created: FN_CALL_SCHEMA_REJECT spike (channel: eng-platform-alerts)
sam: on rollout UX: we should avoid flipping to lenient parsing by default. Instead add a per-route config: schema_mode = [strict|warn|lenient], default strict. For warn mode we still accept the response but emit fncall.schema.warn and tag the response with X-Redwood-Schema-Warn header.
julia: implementation notes: validator currently lives in runtime/validators/fncall_validator.py. We can add a try/except around validation: on failure, consult route config. If strict -> reject and count metric. If warn -> patch tool_output into canonical shape where possible (e.g., if tool_output.summary_text -> result:{text: summary_text}) and continue. If lenient -> attempt best-effort coercion for common mismatches.
kevin: telemetry specifics: sample full payload (payload.sample=true) only for internal SRE/eng role with redaction. Metric names: fncall.schema.reject (counter), fncall.schema.coerce.success (counter), fncall.schema.coerce.failure (counter), fncall.schema.route_fallback (counter). Tagging: route, model, customer_tier, release_commit, config_mode.
elaine: console UX: add a per-route tile showing rejection rate over time with links to sampled logs and the top 5 failure reasons. Also a per-deployment rollout toggle for schema_mode with canary percentages (1%,10%,100%). Add a warning banner when rate > 0.1% for 1min.
qa-bot: test plan: unit tests for coercion rules, e2e using synthetic model responses that return the alternate shapes, and a canary job that runs at 1% traffic for 24h and asserts error rate < threshold.
kevin: security note: storing full tool outputs in telemetry is sensitive. We'll implement a policy: sampled full payloads go to encrypted audit-log with access only to SRE+Security and TTL 30d. Aggregated metrics contain no PII.
marta: rollout plan proposal: 1) add warn mode and metrics (PR by julia) -> canary 1% for 48h; 2) if stable, expand to 10% and enable small coercion rules; 3) after 1 week, decide on default.
julia: I'll pick up the PR. rough ETA: branch + unit tests by end of day tomorrow.
kevin: I'll wire up the metrics and console panel. ETA 2 days.
els: quick question: do we need to change quota/rls? If we coerce and accept more requests, may affect billed tokens.
marta: good call. For warn/lenient we should include a meter tag schema_coerce=true so billing pipeline can either bill as normal or apply adjustments. Add a billing-impact flag in the rollout UI.
ops-bot: scheduled rollout job created: schema-mode-canary-1 (start: 2026-03-19T08:00Z)
kevin: one more caveat: the fallback route must be deterministic to avoid oscillation loops. We'll route to the model pinned in route.fallback_model and increment a counter fncall.schema.route_fallback.
marta: ok team — thanks. Julia please @me on the PR. If we see >1% rejections after warn-canary, we'll revert the runtime change that triggered this.
julia: noted. opening PR in ~2h. :thumbsup:
